title: 2D and 3D Matrices to Study Linear Invadosome Formation and Activity
protocol: Place a piece of parafilm on the work area under a sterile laminar flow hood and disinfect it with 70% ethanol.
Aliquot 20 µL droplets of 1 mg/mL gelatin in a line, spaced approximately 1 cm apart.
Cover each 20 μl gelatin droplet with an autoclaved glass coverslip (12 mm in diameter).
Incubate for 20 min at room temperature.
Protect fluorescent gelatin from light during incubation.
Aliquot 40 µL droplets of 0.5% glutaraldehyde in 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) in a line, each spaced approximately 1 cm below the line of coverslips.
Use gloves and do not inhale.
Transfer each gelatin-coated coverslip to a glutaraldehyde droplet using jeweled forceps.
Incubate the coverslip in glutaraldehyde for 40 min at room temperature.
Protect fluorescent coverslips from light during incubation.
Take a 24-well cell culture plate and fill each well with 500 µL of sterile 1x PBS.
Place the coverslips, gelatin side up, into each well in the plate.
Wash the coverslips twice in 1x PBS for 5 min each.
Use commercial collagen I extracted from rat-tail tendon in 0.02 N acetic acid.
Withdraw the quantity of collagen I necessary to prepare 500 µL of solution per coverslip at a final concentration of 0.4 mg/mL of collagen I.
Add 5-carboxy x rhodamine succinimidyl ester at a final concentration of 10 µg/mL, calculated for the final volume of collagen I solution (n x 500 µL).
Mix the solution by pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Dilute to the final volume with 1X Dulbecco's Phosphate-Buffered Saline (DPBS) containing calcium and magnesium.
Use directly.
Prepare a solution of fluorescent or non-fluorescent collagen I at a final concentration of 0.4 mg/mL in 1X DPBS containing calcium and magnesium.
Add 500 µL of fluorescent or non-fluorescent collagen I solution per coverslip in a 24-well cell culture plate.
Incubate for 4 h at 37 °C for collagen I polymerization.
After incubation, remove the excess collagen I by tilting the plate and pipetting on the side of the well (not directly on the coverslip) to avoid damaging the matrix.
Prepare the cells in the appropriate culture medium.
Plate the cells for 4 hours on collagen I matrix to determine the kinetics of linear invadosome formation and the associated degradation activity.
Incubate the cells for 12 hours on collagen I matrix to quantify the formation of linear invadosomes.
Assess the degradation activity by incubating the cells for 24 hours on collagen I matrix.
Fix the coverslips for 10 min in 500 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde in 1X PBS.
Wash twice with 1x PBS.
Store fixed coverslips at 4 °C, protected from light.
Permeabilize the cells for 10 min with a freshly prepared solution of 0.2% Triton X-100 in 1x PBS.
Wash the coverslips twice with 1x PBS.
Dilute primary antibody in 4% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 1x PBS, as described in the Materials Table.
Aliquot 50 µL droplets of primary antibody solution and place each coverslip on a droplet spaced approximately 1 cm apart.
Incubate for 40 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Wash twice with 1x PBS.
Dilute the secondary antibody, phalloidin, and Hoechst dye in 0.04% BSA in 1x PBS.
Aliquot 50 μL droplets of the mix, spaced approximately 1 cm below the first line of coverslips.
Place each coverslip on a droplet.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Wash twice with 1x PBS.
Wash once with distilled water to remove salts.
Mount the coverslips on a glass slide with polymerizing mounting medium.
Let the coverslips dry overnight at room temperature, protected from light.
Count cells forming linear invadosomes, approximately 100 cells per coverslip.
Use technical triplicates for quantification.
Quantify at least 300 cells per n, with n = 3.
Calculate the percentage of cells forming linear invadosome by averaging three independent experiments.
Take sequential images of F-actin and Tks5 stains using a confocal microscope.
Adapt the macro to a 1,024 x 1,024 image format.
Use ImageJ with the supplementary macro for analysis.
Take 30 images per coverslip of fluorescent gelatin and Hoechst-stained nuclei.
Use three coverslips per condition.
Use ImageJ software as described in Martin KH et al.
Prepare collagen I by cross-linking it with succinimidyl ester dye.
Polymerize the collagen I for 1 hour at 37°C.
Add cells in serum-free medium on top of the collagen I plug.
Place an insert in medium with 10% FBS.
Fix collagen I plugs 1 hour after cell seeding in control conditions.
Fix collagen I plugs 3 days after cell seeding in experimental conditions to determine invasion capacity.
Prepare the collagen I solution on ice under a sterile laminar flow hood.
Aspirate 1 mg of commercial rat-tail collagen I to prepare a solution with a final concentration of 2 mg/mL collagen I.
Add 5-carboxy x Rhodamine succinimidyl ester at a final concentration of 1 µg/mL, calculated for the final volume of collagen I solution (in this case, 500 µL).
Mix well and incubate for 5 min on ice under the sterile laminar flow hood, protected from light.
Add 50 μl of ice-cold, filtered 10X PBS and 6.25 μl of ice-cold 1 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to the solution.
Add sterile water according to the formula 443.75 - x µL of collagen I.
Mix well after adding sterile water.
Add 100 μl of prepared collagen I solution per Boyden chamber insert.
Incubate for 1 h at 37 °C to allow for polymerization.
Add cell culture medium enriched with fetal bovine serum (FBS) into new wells; place inserts into these wells.
Seed 30,000 cells on top of the collagen I plug in FBS-free medium.
Culture the cells at 37 °C.
Fix the collagen I plug for 30 min in 4% paraformaldehyde in 1x PBS.
Permeabilize samples with 0.2% Triton X-100 in 1x PBS for 30 minutes.
Incubate with primary antibody solution for 1.5 hours.
Incubate with secondary antibody solution for 1.5 hours.
Stain for F-actin or nuclei to localize the cells.
Cut around the membrane of the insert using a scalpel.
Transfer the collagen I plug carefully to a glass-bottom dish, ensuring the top of the plug is in contact with the glass.
Attach the insert membrane to the bottom of the collagen I plug to maintain integrity.
Place a coverslip on the collagen I plug and mount with polymerizing mounting medium to prevent drying out.
Image the collagen I plug using an inverted confocal microscope.
Acquire a z-stack from the top to the bottom of the collagen I plug to visualize cell invasion.
Determine the thickness of the z-stack by examining how deeply cells invade the imaging field.
Perform acquisitions with a 40X oil objective in a 512 x 512 format with a z-step size of 0.25 μm.
